challenge.solution:
from sklearn.cluster import KMeans
import numpy as np

X = np.array([[1, 2], [1, 4], [1, 0], [10, 2], [10, 4], [10, 0]])

kmeans = KMeans(n_clusters=3, random_state=42)
kmeans.fit(X)
labels = kmeans.labels_
print(labels)
challenge.hint: Pass n_clusters=3 to the KMeans constructor, then call .fit(X).
challenge.explanation: KMeans will mathematically group the points based on their Euclidean distance, automatically assigning a cluster ID (0, 1, or 2) to each coordinate.

content.title: Dimensionality Reduction: PCA
content.explanation:
• Beginner-friendly explanation.
• It finds the underlying 'principal' patterns and discards the noisy, redundant data.
• Real-world intuition.
• Imagine looking at a complex 3D object like a bicycle.
• Why the concept matters.

content.title: PCA (Principal Component Analysis)
content.explanation: Just like our 3D mug shadow analogy, PCA finds the perfect angle to compress these complex data points into a simple 2D view.

questions.question: Why is standardizing data a strict prerequisite for PCA?
options: PCA is variance-based; features with larger scales will completely dominate the principal components.
It increases the number of dimensions automatically.
It prevents the need for train/test splitting.
questions.explanation: Since PCA seeks to maximize variance, a feature measured in millions (like volume) will mathematically overshadow a feature measured in decimals (like percentages) if not scaled.

content.title: Understanding t-SNE
content.explanation:
• Beginner-friendly explanation.
• Real-world intuition.
• PCA just squashes the bowl flat.
• Why the concept matters.
• Human brains cannot comprehend data in 50 dimensions.

content.title: t-SNE Visualization
content.explanation: See how beautifully t-SNE untangles the messy high-dimensional data into distinct, colorful clusters that our human eyes can instantly recognize.

challenge.explanation: This code demonstrates the full t-SNE workflow: data scaling, model fitting, and visualization. The resulting plot shows how similar digits cluster together in 2D space.
challenge.hint: Remember to scale your data first! Use StandardScaler from sklearn.preprocessing.
challenge.question: Implement t-SNE on the digits dataset
challenge.solution:
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
scaler = StandardScaler()
X_scaled = scaler.fit_transform(X)
t_sne = TSNE(n_components=2, perplexity=30, random_state=42)
X_embedded = t_sne.fit_transform(X_scaled)
plt.scatter(X_embedded[:, 0], X_embedded[:, 1], c=digits.target, cmap='Spectral', alpha=0.6)
plt.show()

questions.question: When should you prefer t-SNE over PCA?

content.title: DBSCAN: Density-Based Clustering
content.explanation:
• Beginner-friendly explanation.
• Real-world intuition.
• Imagine looking at a satellite map of a country at night.
• The brightly lit, densely packed areas are cities (clusters).
• The dark, empty spaces are rural areas (low density).

content.title: Anomaly Detection: Spotting the Outliers
content.explanation:
• Beginner-friendly explanation.
• It learns what 'normal' looks like, so it can flag anything abnormal.
• Real-world intuition.
• Imagine you have a loyal dog who barks every time the mail carrier arrives.
• You're used to this.

content.title: Anomaly Detection: Spotting the Outliers
content.explanation: Most unsupervised learning groups data (clustering). Anomaly Detection focuses on the data points that DO NOT belong to any group. Algorithms like Isolation Forest act as a high-tech security system, learning the shape of 'normal' data and instantly flagging bizarre occurrences.
